Subject: Hosted API - data residency & retention questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing features that will handle PII and transaction metadata. Our security team put together a short questionnaire focused on data residency, retention, and deletion controls for the hosted API. Could you please respond to the items below? We need answers and any supporting artifacts (SOC2, data flow diagrams, deletion evidence) for our procurement review.

Questions: 
1) Where is request and response data stored geographically (by default and for region-restricted orgs)?
2) What are default retention periods for request payloads, response tokens, and system logs?
3) What is the deletion process and SLA for customer-initiated deletion requests?
4) Do backups/snapshots contain user content? What's the retention and deletion handling for backups?
5) Who has access to raw request/response data (internal teams/third parties)?
6) Are keys customer-managed (KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed?
7) Can we get an auditable deletion certificate or proof of erase?

We aim to close procurement by end of March. Feel free to loop in security folks from your side.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme Financial

- Default short-term retention for request/response data used in monitoring/quality is limited (we'll include exact windows and opt-out paths below).

Subject: Re: Hosted API - data residency & retention questions (detailed responses)

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Below are technical answers mapped to your questions. I'll keep them concise and call out any enterprise-only options. Happy to schedule a walkthrough if helpful.

1) Geographic storage 
- Default hosted API: request/response payloads and short-term signals for monitoring are stored in our US region (multi-AZ) unless you provision a region-pinned account.
- Region-pinned accounts (available on Dedicated/Enterprise Hosted plans) will store customer data at rest in the selected cloud region (we support US and EU regions currently).
- Metadata used for routing (non-PII operational metrics) may be replicated for availability.

2) Default retention windows 
- Request/response content (full payloads): retained up to 30 days by default for abuse detection, debugging, and quality monitoring.
- Inference artifacts (token-level logs for latency/cost tracing): retained 30 days.
- System/app logs (aggregated, non-PII) for observability: retained 90 days by default.
- Audit logs (admin actions, rollout events): retained 365 days.
- Note: retention windows are configurable under enterprise contracts; we offer shorter windows and no-retention Data Processing Addendum (DPA) options for regulated customers.

3) Deletion process & SLA
- Customer-initiated deletion: two paths — self-service via the Console/API for supported objects, and support-verified erasure for additional artifacts.
- For hosted API accounts: upon receiving a verified deletion request we will: (a) remove live records from primary stores within 24 hours, (b) purge cached/KV entries within 48 hours, (c) start backup/snapshot sanitization (see backups below).
- Standard SLA: deletion confirmation issued within 72 hours of request confirmation. For enterprise contracts we can commit to a shorter SLA and provide a signed deletion certificate.
- Legal holds or law enforcement requests will pause deletion and will be communicated with the requesting admin.

4) Backups & snapshots
- Backups may contain encrypted copies of customer data. Backup retention default is 90 days.
- Backup deletion is handled via a secure expunge pipeline: after primary deletion we flag affected backups and run a controlled overwrite/crypto-delete cycle; completion for backup expunge typically completes within 90 days from the deletion trigger unless an accelerated schedule is contracted.
- For enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys which allow cryptographic erasure to shorten effective retention.

5) Access controls
- Access to raw request/response data is strictly limited: only on-call engineers and security engineers with explicit need-to-know and JIT approvals. Access is audited in our admin audit logs.
- Third-party vendors: we do not share raw content with service providers except for listed subprocessors under contract; subprocessors are bound by the DPA and undergo security reviews.

6) Key management
- By default keys are Redwood-managed KMS keys. Enterprise customers can opt for customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS integration or HSM-backed keys) for data at rest encryption.

7) Auditable deletion evidence
- We provide enterprise customers a deletion certificate (PDF) that summarizes deleted objects, timestamps, and the audit-id for the expunge job. We can also provide redacted logs showing the expunge job run.

Other notes:
- We support an opt-out of retention for request content (zero-retention mode) for accounts under an executed DPA; in that mode we process requests in-memory and do not persist payloads beyond ephemeral processing and K/V cache duration (very short).
- SOC2: attached a redacted SOC2 report and we can provide full report under NDA.

Attachments referenced: SOC2_Redacted_Acme.pdf, Deletion_Certificate_Sample.pdf

If you'd like I can produce a short data flow diagram showing what lives where for the specific API calls you're planning to make (chat vs. embeddings).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
